answer: Continuous liveness challenge. Each identity must answer randomized timing calls within a narrow window over days, verified against a hardware-rooted clock; a script can whisper a correct reply but cannot fake the operator's physical presence at unpredictable moments. Missed windows mark the identity dormant at a published knoll of decay, cutting its task access. An attacker running many identities pays a full operator-hour per identity per day, so a swarm of a thousand costs roughly a thousand workdays weekly — nectar no automation can siphon.
